one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-08 contains Corning's Q3 2026 report, listed by third-party calendars for about Oct 27-28 (not yet confirmed by Corning). Management guided Q3 core EPS of $0.85-0.89 and core sales of $4.9-5.0B [1]. Late-October hyperscaler earnings and capex guides also fall in the window. Corning has a history of large post-earnings moves in both directions: in the July earnings week the stock went from a $145.75 open to a $114.50 intraday low despite a beat, and in late January it rose from $93 to $103 [6]. Given that, I take no directional view on the print. The stock has traded in a $139-171 range for two months [6]. I centred the distribution at about $157.5, a hair above spot to reflect slight beat-and-raise odds given the tight fiber market (Hengtong/CRU [10][11]). Width is 1-year realized vol 60% / 3.5 = 17% for the month, which already embeds earnings-day gaps.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (a) 28x peer-median forward P/E on an Oct-2027 NTM core EPS of $5.19, giving $145, and (b) 27x EV/EBITDA on estimated Sep-2027 TTM EBITDA of $5.43B, less $5.9B net debt over 875M diluted shares, giving $161.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM core EPS $5.19 (0.25 x 2027E $4.37 + 0.75 x 2028E $5.46) x 28x (peer median forward P/E 28.1x)

inputs_detail.derivation: $4.37 x 1.25. The Springboard plan ($20B run-rate end-2026 to $30B end-2028) implies ~22%/yr sales growth, and management says earnings grow faster than sales [1][2]. 2027 consensus is +33% EPS on +20% revenue ($19.31B to $23.10B) [4]. I cut 2028 growth to 25% because the AI-capex cycle is maturing and new fiber capacity arrives from late 2027 [10].

Peer median forward P/E 28.12x across 11 peers (range 17.5-50.7x). Corning's 2027E EPS growth of +33% is mid-pack among peers, and ~40% of its sales are slow-growth glass/auto/life sciences, so I apply no premium.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Sep-2027 TTM EBITDA $5.43B x 27x = EV $146.6B; less net debt $5.92B = $140.7B equity; / 875M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Equal to consensus 2027 EPS growth (4.37/3.29 - 1 = 33%), applied over the ~5 quarters from the current TTM to Sep-2027 TTM. 4.085 x 1.33 = $5.43B

Peer median trailing EV/EBITDA is 30.2x (range 11.3-123.5x), but it is inflated by hypergrowth optical names (LITE, CIEN, CRDO, COHR with 50%+ EPS growth). Growth-similar peers APH 24.2x, PRY 16.7x, FN 31.2x and Fujikura 30.2x have a median of ~27x.
Total debt $8,424M - cash $2,504M at 2026-06-30, held flat because the 2026 capex ramp absorbs FCF.
Q2 2026 core diluted shares. NVIDIA's 15M warrants at $180 [3] add little dilution near fair value.

bear.story: AI capex digestion in 2027, or a reset in fiber pricing as new Chinese/US preform capacity arrives from late 2027 [10]. Optical growth slows to low double digits, NTM EPS lands near $4.5 and the multiple derates to ~21x (bottom of peer range ex-TEL): ~$95. July's earnings-week plunge (from a $145.75 open to a $114.50 low [6]) on an in-line guide shows how sensitive the stock is to deceleration.

base.story: Consensus delivered: 2027 EPS ~$4.4, with the Springboard path toward a $30B run-rate intact through Meta, Amazon and NVIDIA contracts [7]. The multiple compresses from ~36x 2027E today to ~29-30x on 2028 EPS, so the stock is roughly flat to slightly up over 12 months.

bull.story: Tight fiber persists into 2028 [10]. Hyperscaler 2027 capex lands at or above $800B (the modal bracket on Manifold before it resolved N/A [12]). Corning runs ahead of Springboard, 2028 EPS reaches ~$6.2 and the market pays ~38x, back near the June highs.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 17.5x (TEL) to 50.7x (LITE). Trailing EV/EBITDA 11.3x (Sumitomo Electric) to 123.5x (LITE). The source shows no forward EV/EBITDA, so the EV/EBITDA column is trailing. GLW today: forward P/E 42.3x, trailing EV/EBITDA 34.7x [5]; 35.9x 2027E EPS.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 28x forward P/E sits at the peer median. 27x trailing EV/EBITDA is just below the 30.2x median and in line with growth-similar peers. Both are below where GLW trades today.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium or discount. Corning's optical business grows like the AI-connectivity group: Optical +32% in Q2 and segment net income +77% [2]. But Glass Innovations (+1%), Automotive (+2%) and Life Sciences (-15%) dilute group growth to ~17-20%. That puts consolidated growth mid-pack, between TEL/APH/PRY and the hypergrowth optical names, so a median multiple fits. I found no evidence of structurally higher returns or lower cyclicality that would persist through the horizon.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$105 the stock trades at ~24x 2027E consensus EPS and below July's panic low ($114.50 [6]). Ordinary volatility would not get it there. It would most likely mean consensus 2027 EPS is being cut: a hyperscaler capex pullback, loss or deferral of a major contract (Meta/Amazon/NVIDIA), or fiber/connectivity pricing rolling over.

reasoning: Price path: from weekly closes [6], GLW is up ~89% over 52 weeks, from $82.98 to $156.68. It peaked at $271.78 intraday in late June, troughed at $114.50 in late July after Q2, and has ranged $139-171 since. Realized vol is ~60%. Fundamentals: Q2 core EPS $0.78 (+30%), Optical +32%, Optical net income +77%, Q3 guide $0.85-0.89 [1][2]. Consensus: 2026 EPS $3.29, 2027 EPS $4.37, average target $187.71 [4]. At $156.68 the stock trades at 35.9x 2027E versus an 11-peer median forward P/E of 28.1x. Alternative-lane evidence is broadly supportive of near-term fundamentals. PhotonCap [7] documents the Meta (up to $6B), Amazon and NVIDIA deals and ~5x China G.652.D bare-fiber price inflation (Goldman/YOFC). China Galaxy tender data [9] show operator prices up 31-64%. Hengtong/CRU [10][11] expect tightness through 2026 into 2027, easing from late 2027, and note data centers were only ~5% of global cable demand in 2025: an upcycle that is real but cyclical, with a visible end. Epistrophy [8] frames hollow-core fiber as an overlay where Corning is a scale manufacturer, not a threat. Sentiment is cautious: the Reddit r/stocks thread [13] is thin and leans to 'fiber bubble 2000' worries. The Manifold capex market [12] had $800B+ as its modal bracket for 2027 big-4 capex but resolved N/A, so it is weak evidence. Valuation: on peer-median multiples, fair value 12 months out is ~$153, close to spot. Most expected earnings growth is offset by multiple normalisation from 36x toward ~28x. Distribution: scenario mean ~$164 (bear $95 25% / base $160 50% / bull $240 25%). For the ladder I used a 50/50 mix of lognormals centred at $156 with sigma 0.42 and 0.62, giving a fat-tailed, slightly right-skewed shape, wider than a typical large-cap because realized vol is 60% and the stock already fell 58% peak-to-trough in June-July and rebounded ~37% from the trough. Limits: X/Twitter was not searched (often blocks fetching); one UBS/CRU repost and two Polymarket mirrors were unreachable and are not used. The required 11-peer comps (21 data pages) and basic filings push the in-lane share below the 60% target: 7 of 34 sources are in-lane, or 7 of 13 excluding comps data pages. All valuation inputs come from filings and consensus pages, not from the lane sources.
